title: Certificate for Orthogonal Equivalence of Real Polynomials by Polynomial-Weighted Principal Component Analysis
summary: Suppose that $f(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ and $g(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ are two real polynomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables. If the polynomials $f$ and $g$ are the same up to orthogonal symmetry a natural question is then what element of the orthogonal group induces the orthogonal symmetry; i.e. to find the element $R\in O(n)$ such that $f(Rx)=g(x)$.
